rubricSource.statement: The dispositions below are measured against each finding's own requiredRepair field, not against this adjudicator's opinion and not against the review's prose summary.
rubricSource.RPPV2-PF-01.requiredRepair: Publish a successor with a closed per-operator grammar: exact required/optional fields, operand/reference grammar and types, comparison domains, action read/write semantics and atomicity, rule/event-selector records, precheck semantics, invariant evaluation and invariant-failure consequence. Make an independent interpreter derivable from that JSON alone and add structural/adversarial mutations for every grammar fork.
rubricSource.RPPV2-PF-02.requiredRepair: Either narrow the context domain to exact admissible combinations and bind every missing D9 input, or add host-owned normalized cause/settled-result custody sufficient to derive one complete D9 axis record and exact HostTermination for every admitted context. Signal-after must carry or reference the immutable settled result; host faults and deficiencies must have exact identities; VERIFIED_CANCELLED must be total. The checker must recompute D9 outputs for the full admitted domain and reject DEFER/PRESERVE placeholders as final results.

verdictSummary.statement: Both blockers are discharged on their own stated rubrics, measured by construction. The Rust substrate is NOT unimplementable and this is not an architecture blocker. What remains is a governance/record defect in IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md and IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md -- neither records that the base they pin carries a standing independent REJECT -- plus three non-blocking observations recorded below.
verdictSummary.whyThisIsNotADischargeOfConvenience: The decisive evidence is negative-space: each blocker's DEFECTIVE surfaces were located, and every one of them is a member of a replacedSelectors list and therefore does not survive the merge. No inherited selector was ever a blocking surface. This was verified selector-by-selector, not inferred from any artifact's self-description.

Start from the exact parsed v2 object; take the 18 inheritedTopLevelSelectors verbatim; drop the 8 replacedSelectors; overlay the v4 sections. The same was done for both joins.

protocolMerge.schemaLanguageV4Standing: schemaLanguageV4 is an ADDITIVE overlay: /schemaLanguage is NOT in replacedSelectors, so v2's schemaLanguage survives verbatim and schemaLanguageV4 is added alongside it. Measured: the two objects share ZERO key names (v2 has maps/arrays/integer/text/bytes/external/union; v4 has closedMap/taggedUnion/exactType/array/referencePathGrammar/recursiveBounds/artifactFailure/runtimeFailure). There is therefore no collision and no precedence question to resolve. check-rust-provider-protocol-v4.py line 530 enumerates schemaLanguageV4 in its exact expected_root key list and validates its exact field set, so the overlay is mechanically bound, not incidental.
protocolMerge.selectorValueBinding: The protocol overlay binds inheritance by whole-file v2 digest (6308a98c...) plus the ordered 18-name list only. It publishes NO per-selector commitments. Value equality is nonetheless guaranteed because the whole-file digest pins every selector value. See observation OBS-3.

findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.title: check-rust-provider-protocol-v4.py's ripgrep dependency is inherited from the REJECTED v2 checker, and its absence produces a misleading non-zero exit
findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.measured: check-rust-provider-protocol-v4.py itself imports no subprocess and no shutil -- grep for subprocess/shutil.which/'rg' over it returns nothing. The dependency is TRANSITIVE: v4_replay imports and runs check-rust-provider-protocol-v2.py, whose aggregate_manifest at line 1377 executes subprocess.run(['rg','--files','docs/coop/artifacts'], check=True). On this host 'rg' resolves only as a zsh shell function (from a shell snapshot); shutil.which('rg') returns None; real ripgrep binaries exist at /Users/sb/.pi/agent/bin/rg (ripgrep 15.1.0) and inside /Applications/ChatGPT.app, neither on PATH.
findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.consequence: Run without a real rg on PATH, the checker exits 1 with FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'rg' and a Python traceback -- BEFORE evaluating a single contract property. A reader applying 'non-zero exit means a guard fired' would record a false failure of the Rust protocol. With /Users/sb/.pi/agent/bin on PATH it exits 0 in both modes.
findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.secondOrderPoint: The freeze section 7.3 evidence for RUST-PROVIDER-PROTOCOL is therefore not reproducible on a clean machine without an external, unpinned, unhashed binary -- and the call site sits inside the REJECTED v2 checker, reachable only through the retained replay that freeze section 2 rule 5 authorises.

Measured: every defective surface of both blockers is a replaced selector; not one of the 18 inherited selectors was ever a blocking surface; and the v2 review's own effect clause is scoped to 'the five-file v2 set', which the merged contract is not. But the protocol is the single place where selector-level drift could not be localised from published bytes, and it is the largest of the three inherited sets.

Only 23 of those 41 selectors have a published commitment in the candidate to match against; the 18 protocol ones have none. The boolean is presumably true of the reviewer's own recomputation against the whole-file pin, which is sound, but it is not independently re-checkable from published bytes for the protocol third.

findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.title: PF-01's citation of #/schemaLanguage/maps is a yardstick citation, not a defect citation -- and this is the specific point on which the blind litmus's inference fails
findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.measured: The finding reads: 'The protocol's own schemaLanguage says a closed map has exact required and optional fields, but transitionAstV2 supplies no such grammar for these records.' schemaLanguage is the standard; transitionAstV2 is the thing that failed it. The inference 'schemaLanguage is inherited unreplaced, therefore the overlay does not touch the thing the blocker is about' does not follow: the overlay was never required to change the yardstick, only to satisfy it.
findingsNeitherTheLitmusNorTheCoordinato.corroboration: Independently, v2's schemaLanguage and v4's schemaLanguageV4 share zero key names, so the inherited yardstick is neither overridden nor contradicted -- it stands, and the merged AST now meets it at 0 inventions.

whatIDidNotCheck: I did not re-review the v4 candidate. This is not an independent review of rust-provider-protocol.v4.json and creates no verdict for it.

I did not re-derive or re-validate the seven v1 findings (RPP-PF-01..07) or the twenty retained binding-gap forks (RPP-GAP-01..20) beyond noting that the v2 review tied RPP-GAP-09 to PF-01 and RPP-GAP-19 to PF-02. Whether those two retained gaps are themselves closed at v4 is outside this adjudication.

I did not verify the 12,288-tuple supervisor reducer, the 78 FSM traces, the 522 phase/event totality comparisons, the 187 nominal-type probes, the 263 v2 semantic-positive checks or the 68 v2 adversarial checks independently. I observed the checkers report them and the v4 review report matching counts; I reproduced only the finalizer domain (2304/148/2156) and the AST grammar closure myself.

I did not independently recompute admittedTupleCommitment (sha256:bfdecd8a...) or invalidCombinations.tupleCommitment (sha256:28d92cee...). RPPV3-PF-03 was about exactly that encoding; I relied on the v4 review's independent closure of RPPV3-PF-03 rather than re-deriving the 35,347 admitted bytes.

I did not verify the 47 allowedReferencePaths resolve against the actual state/event/limits records, nor that the 28 rules are collectively total over the phase/event space -- the checker's fsm_totality=522 asserts it and I did not reproduce it.
I did not execute check-rust-provider-protocol-v2.py or -v3.py standalone, only transitively via the v4 checker's retained replay.

I did not audit whether /Users/sb/.pi/agent/bin/rg is the same ripgrep the original evidence was produced with. It is unpinned and unhashed by any artifact; I recorded only that it is ripgrep 15.1.0 arm64 and that its presence flips the v4 checker from traceback-exit-1 to exit-0.

I did not evaluate the D9 contract gaps the freeze already names (observation-to-faultCause selection, optional-field presence policy, the success/policy-failed/interrupted branch) as anything other than pre-existing recorded residuals. I did not test whether they affect the 148 finalizer contexts.
I did not assess DELIVERY, RESOLVED-INPUTS, EVIDENCE, C-2 or any other contract head. The stale d9-exit-contract.v1.13 pin in evidence.v10 is noted by the freeze and was not examined here.
I did not check any product-level or claim-register consequence. CD-RT-5 was not evaluated and remains BLOCKED_ON_PHASE_1A.
nonClaims: This artifact applies nothing, seals nothing, freezes nothing and changes no status field of any other artifact.
It is not an independent review and does not satisfy any review obligation.
It does not supersede rust-provider-protocol.v2.review-independent-prefreeze.json. That REJECT stands as the verdict on the five-file v2 set.
It does not authorise applying the v4 five-file set, which remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED and requires the section 3.2 item 7 all-five application rule.
It grants no normative standing to rust-provider-protocol.v2.json beyond what freeze section 3.2 item 5 already asserts.

requiredNextAction.forTheCoordinator: Both blockers are discharged on substance, so no Rust successor is required before signature on account of RPPV2-PF-01/-02. What IS required is a record correction: no artifact formally closes either id, and neither IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md nor IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md records that the base they pin carries a standing independent REJECT. Recommended: (a) a successor or coordinator closure naming RPPV2-PF-01 and RPPV2-PF-02 and recording their discharge against the replaced selectors; (b) a freeze note reconciling section 2 rule 3 with section 3.2 item 5 for the inherited-selector case, which rule 5 does not cover; (c) record OBS-1 so the ripgrep dependency is not mistaken for a Rust-protocol failure.
requiredNextAction.explicitlyNotRecommended: Halting Rust implementation. The measured evidence does not support treating the Rust substrate as an architecture blocker.
